The trace simulates controlled probes (one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, periodic_D) and tournament opponents. It proposes changes: unconditional final-round defection, conditional penultimate-round cooperation against reciprocators, and cautious exploitation of non-retaliatory cooperators.

STRATEGY: The parent is a conditional endgame-defecting strategy (defects when n>=97 and cooperation rate >0.7). The trace simulates its behaviour against the listed probe strategies (one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, periodic_D) and other population slots, computing payoffs for defecting vs cooperating in the last rounds. It considers changing the parent to defect earlier (last 3-6 rounds) or to add a probe/test defection at n=20 or n=90 to detect forgiving opponents and exploit them.

STRATEGY: The parent plays a TFT-with-forgiveness strategy that cooperates by default, retaliates against frequent defection, and probes at rounds 20/40/60/80 by defecting once when the opponent has been perfectly cooperative. It simulates the probe/exploit outcomes against the listed population strategies (slot1–slot11, parent, AllD, AllC, TFT variants) and computes expected gains. It changes the strategy by adding adaptive probing and exploitation: after a probe, it cooperates once to test, then continues defecting if the opponent forgave, or resumes cooperation if the opponent retaliated.
